title: Selected work
intro: Eight bold months, a yellow house, and more finished canvases than anyone expected. This corridor holds interfaces, identities and one poster.
cue: Keep scrolling — the gallery runs sideways

works.title: Fraemerate
works.note: A mark made of five ribbons, because the studio's whole argument is that restraint still has movement in it.
works.description: Identity and site for a small digital product studio. The mark is five kinked bands stacked into a diamond — a rippling frame — and the rest of the system is built to stay out of its way.
works.outcome: A live studio site at fraemerate.com, built on the same mark.
works.alt: The Fraemerate studio mark: five ribbon-like bands stacked into a diamond, each kinked in the middle, in bone white on a near-black ground.

works.title: Google-Themed Portfolio
works.note: Everyone already knows how to read a results page. I borrowed the reading, not the styling.
works.description: A portfolio built as a search results page: the query is my name, and the answers are the work. Overview, Projects, Skills, Achievements and Contact become result tabs, and a knowledge panel carries the facts nobody wants a paragraph for.
works.outcome: A complete design concept, published while still in progress.
works.alt: A portfolio designed to look like a Google search results page: the search field reads "koyal borbora", and the results are a name, a role, tab pills, a photograph, a project card and knowledge-panel cards for birth date and education.

works.title: On-Demand Mechanic
works.note: The hard part was never the booking. It was the twelve minutes of not knowing where anybody is.
works.description: A live-tracking app for roadside car repair: watch the mechanic approach on the map, see them arrive, then follow the job through Reached, Inspection and Repair. Most of the design sits in the states between those moments.
works.outcome: A booking-to-handover flow carried through to high fidelity, in a light and a dark treatment.
works.alt: Three phone screens for an on-demand mechanic app on a teal ground: a live map tracking the mechanic to your location with a call button, and two versions of the arrival screen showing a job timeline of Reached, Inspection and Repair.

works.title: PlaySync
works.note: A bracket is a data structure before it is a screen. I drew the structure first.
works.description: Tournament management for someone standing at the side of a pitch rather than sitting at a desk: fixtures, brackets, live scoring and standings, all reachable with one thumb.
works.outcome: A connected set of organiser and player screens covering setup, live scoring and standings.
works.alt: A tournament management interface: an eight-team knockout bracket across a deep blue ground resolving to a gold winner slot, with a live score card showing Team C leading Team H three to one.

works.title: Diffusion.img
works.note: The interesting problem was not the output. It was giving someone a way to steer.
works.description: An interface for text-to-image generation, designed around iteration rather than a single lucky result: write the prompt, compare what comes back, keep the seed that worked.
works.outcome: Prompt, generation and comparison screens, taken through to high fidelity.
works.alt: An AI image generation interface on a near-black ground: a prompt field, a Generate button, four resulting images, and a settings panel listing model, steps, guidance, seed and size.

works.title: Weather App
works.note: The first thing I ever published. I can see every seam, and I am leaving it up.
works.description: A weather interface built around the forecast rather than the current temperature — the question people are usually actually asking when they open one.
works.outcome: My first published project, and the one everything after it was measured against.
works.alt: A mobile weather app interface: a large temperature over Jorhat, Assam, an hourly strip along the middle, and a five-day forecast shown as temperature bars rather than a list.

works.title: Red Bull Poster
works.note: An interface gets a second chance to explain itself. A poster gets one.
works.description: An unbriefed poster study: composition, energy, and making a single image carry the whole message with no interface to fall back on.
works.outcome: A finished key visual, built for social and print crops.
works.alt: A promotional poster study: a can centred on a deep blue ground with gold rays radiating behind it, and the words GIVES YOU WINGS in heavy display type.
